docs.text: HardFOC driver · ESP32 WS2812 RMT Driver ¶ A C++ driver for WS2812 and WS2812B addressable LEDs (NeoPixels) on the ESP32 family. It keeps a pixel buffer, scales brightness, encodes every bit as an RMT symbol and lets the RMT peripheral time the pulses, so the CPU never bit-bangs the line. Animation effects and multi-strip coordination come with it. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver is ESP-IDF code. Unlike the other HardFOC drivers it has no platform port: it calls ESP-IDF's RMT driver directly, so it runs on ESP32 chips with an RMT peripheral and ESP-IDF v5.3 or later, and nowhere else. Porting explains what that means for other targets. WS2812Strip owns an RMT channel, the pixel buffer and the timing; SetPixel() and Show() are the whole loop. See the API guide . Hardware timing. docs.text: API guide ¶ How to do the common jobs with the driver: create a strip, set pixels, dim, resize, animate, drive several strips and handle errors. Every snippet on this page is compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/api_tasks.cpp , where Grb(r, g, b) packs a colour as 0xGGRRBB (see Colour order ). The API reference lists every member. The shape of the API ¶ Class Header Owns WS2812Strip ws2812_cpp.hpp One RMT channel, the pixel buffer, brightness, timing, LED type WS2812Animator ws2812_effects.hpp One effect on one strip: a step counter and a colour WS2812MultiAnimator ws2812_multi_animator.hpp One animator per strip, with a shared step ws2812::RmtTx rmt_wrapper.hpp An RMT transmit channel; raw symbols or WS2812 bytes WS2812Strip member Does WS2812Strip(gpio, channel, num_leds, type, t0h, t1h, t0l, t1l, brightness) Creates the RMT channel; every argument has a Kconfig default SetPixel(index, colour) Writes one pixel of the buffer; out-of-range indices are ignored Show() Scales, encodes and sends the buffer; blocks until done; returns esp_err_t SetBrightness(0-255) Global scale applied at the next Show() SetNumLeds(n) Resizes and clears the buffer SetTimings(t0h, t1h, t0l, t1l) New bit timing in 100 ns ticks Length() The number of LEDs ColorWheel(0-255) A colour on a red-green-blue wheel, packed 0xRRGGBB Begin() Nothing; returns ESP_OK (the constructor already set the channel up) GetDriverVersion() The version string, for example "1.0.0" Create a strip ¶ // WS2812B timing in 100 ns ticks: T0H 400 ns, T1H 800 ns, T0L 900 ns, T1L 500 ns. WS2812Strip make_status_strip () { return WS2812Strip ( GPIO_NUM_8 , // data pin -1 , // channel: ignored, ESP-IDF picks a free one 16 , // LEDs LedType :: RGB , // 24 bits per LED (LedType::RGBW: 32) 4 , 8 , 9 , 5 , // T0H, T1H, T0L, T1L in ticks 64 ); // brightness 0-255 } The constructor creates and enables the RMT channel at once, so create strips where an abort at start-up is acceptable, typically in app_main() or a task's set-up. Keep the object alive as long as you use the LEDs: the destructor releases the channel. The channel argument is accepted and ignored; ESP-IDF's RMT driver picks a free transmit channel. Set pixels and show them ¶ esp_err_t show_gradient ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { const uint32_t n = strip . Length (); const uint32_t last = n > 1 ? n - 1 : 1 ; for ( uint32_t i = 0 ; i < n ; ++ i ) { const auto level = static_cast < uint8_t > ( 255 * i / last ); strip . SetPixel ( i , Grb ( level , 0 , 255 - level )); // blue to red } return strip . Show (); // nothing reaches the LEDs until Show() } SetPixel() only writes the buffer. Show() sends the whole strip every time; there is no partial update, and the LEDs keep their colours until the next frame. Dim the strip ¶ esp_err_t dim ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { strip . SetBrightness ( 16 ); // scales every channel of every LED at the next Show() return strip . Show (); } Each channel is scaled as value × brightness / 255 while encoding. The buffer keeps the full values, so raising the brightness again restores the colours exactly. At low brightness, small values round down to 0. Change the length ¶ esp_err_t grow ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { strip . SetNumLeds ( 60 ); // all pixels are cleared to 0 strip . SetPixel ( 59 , Grb ( 0 , 0 , 255 )); return strip . Show (); } SetNumLeds() reallocates the pixel and symbol buffers and clears every pixel. Call it from the task that calls Show() . Change the timing ¶ void use_ws2812_original_timing ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { // 4, 8, 9, 5 already fit both parts. To centre on the WS2812's nominal 350 / 700 / 800 / 600 ns: strip . SetTimings ( 4 , 7 , 8 , 6 ); // T0H, T1H, T0L, T1L in ticks of 100 ns } The values are RMT ticks of 100 ns. Signal timing has the windows for the WS2812 and WS2812B. Animate ¶ void led_task ( void * arg ) { auto & strip = * static_cast < WS2812Strip *> ( arg ); WS2812Animator anim ( strip ); anim . SetEffect ( WS2812Animator :: Effect :: Rainbow ); for (;;) { anim . Tick (); // computes one frame and calls strip.Show() vTaskDelay ( pdMS_TO_TICKS ( 20 )); } } Effect Each Tick() Off Clears the strip SolidColor Sets every LED to the colour Rainbow Spreads ColorWheel() over the strip and shifts it by one step Chase Lights every third LED and moves the pattern by one Blink Alternates between the colour and off Breath Ramps the strip brightness up and down in steps of 4 (overwrites SetBrightness() ) Larson One lit LED that moves end to end and back Every Tick() ends with a Show() , so the tick rate is the frame rate; 20 ms (50 Hz) is smooth. Tick() ignores the result of Show() ; check transmit errors on the strip if you need them. SetVirtualLength() stretches an effect over a longer imaginary strip, and SetStep() / Step() read and set its position. Drive several strips ¶ void two_strips ( WS2812Strip & front , WS2812Strip & rear ) { // unified = true: both strips run the effect over the longer strip's length. // sync = true: one step counter for both. WS2812MultiAnimator multi ({ & front , & rear }, true , true ); multi . SetEffect ( WS2812Animator :: Effect :: Chase , Grb ( 255 , 80 , 0 )); multi . SetEffect ( 1 , WS2812Animator :: Effect :: Blink , Grb ( 255 , 0 , 0 )); // rear strip only for ( int frame = 0 ; frame < 500 ; ++ frame ) { multi . Tick (); vTaskDelay ( pdMS_TO_TICKS ( 50 )); } } Each strip has its own RMT channel, so the number of strips is limited by the chip's transmit channels ( Porting ). The strips are sent one after the other in each Tick() . Handle errors ¶ bool show_or_report ( WS2812Strip & strip ) { const esp_err_t err = strip . Show (); if ( err != ESP_OK ) { // The RMT driver's code, for example ESP_ERR_INVALID_STATE when the channel is not enabled. ESP_LOGE ( "leds" , "Show failed: %s" , esp_err_to_name ( err )); return false ; } return true ; } Signal Meaning What to do Abort in the RmtTx constructor rmt_new_tx_channel() , rmt_enable() or the encoder failed: no free channel, bad GPIO, no memory Fix the configuration; it is not recoverable at run time Show() returns an esp_err_t other than ESP_OK The RMT driver refused the transfer Log it with esp_err_to_name() ; the frame was not sent Wrong colours, all white, flicker Timing, colour order or signal level, not a software error Troubleshooting Send bytes directly ¶ esp_err_t send_raw_grb ( ws2812 :: RmtTx & tx ) { // Bytes go out as they are, MSB first, with the WS2812B timing built into RmtTx (10 MHz // resolution). const uint8_t frame [] = { 0x00 , 0xFF , 0x00 , // LED 0: red (G, R, B) 0xFF , 0x00 , 0x00 }; // LED 1: green return tx . TransmitWs2812 ( frame , sizeof ( frame )); } ws2812::RmtTx can also be used on its own: TransmitWs2812() sends bytes as they are with the WS2812B timing, Transmit() sends prepared symbols and TransmitBytes() takes your own 0 and 1 symbols. All three block until the transfer is done. The C interface ¶ Do not use ws2812_control.h in new code The C functions ws2812_control_init() , ws2812_write_leds() and ws2812_set_brightness() drive one strip sized by Kconfig. In this version ws2812_write_leds() passes its buffer of RMT symbols to a byte encoder, so the strip receives the bytes of the symbols instead of the colours. Use WS2812Strip . Threads ¶ The classes are not thread-safe. Give each strip one owner task, or guard every call on a strip (and on any animator that uses it) with one mutex.

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is put together: the layers from your application to the LEDs, what each owns, and how one frame reaches the strip. From pixels to pulses, on ESP-IDF Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application, the only code you write, either runs an effect or sets pixels itself. The effects (WS2812Animator and WS2812MultiAnimator, the Effect values listed from inc/ws2812_effects.hpp) draw into a WS2812Strip. The strip (inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp, public methods listed) keeps the pixel buffer, applies the brightness and turns every bit into one RMT symbol with the configured high and low times. ws2812::RmtTx (inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp) owns one RMT transmit channel at 10 MHz and sends the symbols, blocking until they are out. Below it is ESP-IDF's RMT driver (the calls listed from rmt_wrapper.hpp) and the RMT peripheral, which times the pulses on the GPIO that feeds the first LED. Drawn from: inc/ws2812_effects.hpp WS2812Animator::Effect ; inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp WS2812Strip ; inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp ws2812::RmtTx ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . The layers ¶ Layer Where You change it when Effects : WS2812Animator , WS2812MultiAnimator ws2812_effects.hpp , ws2812_multi_animator.hpp You want a new effect Strip : WS2812Strip ws2812_cpp.hpp , ws2812_cpp.cpp Never, for a new board RMT channel : ws2812::RmtTx rmt_wrapper.hpp Never ESP-IDF RMT driver and the peripheral ESP-IDF, esp_driver_rmt Never Each layer uses only the one below it. There is no communication interface for you to implement. The other HardFOC drivers talk to a chip over a bus your port provides; a WS2812 has no bus, only a pulse train with 100 ns resolution, and the RMT peripheral is what makes that possible on an ESP32 without blocking the CPU. Porting explains the consequences. How one frame reaches the strip ¶ sequenceDiagram participant A as Application participant S as WS2812Strip participant T as RmtTx participant R as ESP-IDF RMT A->>S: SetPixel(i, colour), for each LED A->>S: Show() S->>S: scale by brightness, one symbol per bit S->>T: Transmit(symbols, count) T->>R: rmt_transmit(copy encoder) T->>R: rmt_tx_wait_all_done() R-->>T: ESP_OK when the last symbol is out T-->>S: esp_err_t S-->>A: esp_err_t Show() blocks the calling task for the whole frame: about 31 µs per RGB LED with the WS2812B timing ( Signal timing ). The RMT sends the symbols on its own; the CPU only refills the channel's symbol memory from an interrupt. Design choices ¶ Symbols built in software, sent with a copy encoder. Show() writes one rmt_symbol_word_t per bit into a buffer the strip owns, then the RMT copies them out. The timing is plain data, so SetTimings() takes effect at the next Show() and the host tests can check every pulse. One RMT channel per strip, created in the constructor. A strip is ready as soon as it exists; Begin() is kept for older code and returns ESP_OK . Failures to create the channel abort, through ESP_ERROR_CHECK ( Troubleshooting ). Brightness at send time. Pixels are stored unscaled; brightness is applied while encoding, so dimming and restoring never loses colour resolution in the buffer. Effects are separate. The strip knows nothing about animation. An animator draws one frame per Tick() and calls Show() ; you decide when to tick. Heap at construction, not per frame. The strip allocates its pixel and symbol buffers ( std::vector ) when it is created or resized; Show() does not allocate. The C interface ¶ inc/ws2812_control.h is an older C interface for one strip whose length, LED type and timing are fixed by Kconfig. It does not share code with WS2812Strip and it currently sends the wrong data (see the warning in the API guide ); use the C++ classes. docs.text: Symbols built in software, sent with a copy encoder. Show() writes one rmt_symbol_word_t per bit into a buffer the strip owns, then the RMT copies them out. The timing is plain data, so SetTimings() takes effect at the next Show() and the host tests can check every pulse. One RMT channel per strip, created in the constructor. A strip is ready as soon as it exists; Begin() is kept for older code and returns ESP_OK . Failures to create the channel abort, through ESP_ERROR_CHECK ( Troubleshooting ). Brightness at send time. Pixels are stored unscaled; brightness is applied while encoding, so dimming and restoring never loses colour resolution in the buffer. Effects are separate. The strip knows nothing about animation. An animator draws one frame per Tick() and calls Show() ; you decide when to tick. Heap at construction, not per frame. The strip allocates its pixel and symbol buffers ( std::vector ) when it is created or resized; Show() does not allocate.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ The Kconfig options and constructor arguments that set a strip's pin, length, LED type, timing and brightness. Kconfig ¶ The component adds the menu HF-ESP32-WS2812-RMT Configuration to idf.py menuconfig . Its values are the defaults of the WS2812Strip constructor and the fixed settings of the C interface. Option Default Meaning CONFIG_WS2812_LED_TYPE_RGB / _RGBW RGB 24 or 32 bits per LED CONFIG_WS2812_NUM_LEDS 8 Number of LEDs CONFIG_WS2812_LED_RMT_TX_GPIO 18 Data pin CONFIG_WS2812_LED_RMT_TX_CHANNEL -1 Ignored: ESP-IDF chooses the channel CONFIG_WS2812_T0H 14 0 bit high time, in ticks CONFIG_WS2812_T1H 52 1 bit high time, in ticks CONFIG_WS2812_T0L 52 0 bit low time, in ticks CONFIG_WS2812_T1L 52 1 bit low time, in ticks CONFIG_WS2812_DEFAULT_BRIGHTNESS 255 0 to 255 Every option is the default of the matching WS2812Strip constructor argument. The LED type, count, timing and brightness are also the fixed settings of the C interface. The default timing is not WS2812B timing WS2812Strip counts in ticks of 100 ns. The defaults 14, 52, 52 and 52 mean 1.4 µs and 5.2 µs, which a WS2812B reads as all ones. Pass the timing to the constructor, as every example on this site does, or set the options to the values below. docs.text: Hardware ¶ What to connect between an ESP32 and a WS2812B strip, the signal it expects, and how to power it. The numbers here come from the Worldsemi WS2812B datasheet and, for the original WS2812, the WS2812 datasheet . Clones and later revisions differ; check the datasheet of the LEDs you bought. Pins ¶ Pin Name Connect to 1 VDD 5 V supply (3.5 V to 5.3 V) 2 DOUT (out) DIN of the next LED 3 VSS Supply ground and ESP32 ground 4 DIN (in) ESP32 GPIO, through a level shifter A strip brings out VDD (often labelled 5V or +), DIN and GND at its input end. The data goes one way: connect the end marked DIN or with the arrow pointing away from the connector. The ESP32 side ¶ Setting Value Notes Peripheral One RMT transmit channel Chosen by ESP-IDF's RMT driver; the channel argument is ignored GPIO Any output-capable GPIO GPIO8 in the examples (ESP32-C6) Resolution 10 MHz, 100 ns per tick Fixed by WS2812Strip Symbol memory 64 symbols, no DMA Refilled by interrupt while a frame is sent Output level 3.3 V Below the WS2812B's 3.5 V high threshold at 5 V Signal ¶ The LEDs read one line, non-return-to-zero at 800 kbit/s. Every bit is a high pulse followed by a low one; the length of the high pulse decides 0 or 1. Each LED keeps the first 24 bits it receives and passes the rest on through DOUT, reshaped. A low line for longer than the reset time latches the new colours into every LED. Parameter WS2812B Driver (100 ns ticks) T0H, 0 bit high 0.40 µs ±150 ns 4: 0.4 µs T1H, 1 bit high 0.80 µs ±150 ns 8: 0.8 µs T0L, 0 bit low 0.85 µs ±150 ns 9: 0.9 µs T1L, 1 bit low 0.45 µs ±150 ns 5: 0.5 µs TH + TL 1.25 µs ±600 ns 1.3 µs Reset, line low more than 50 µs not sent ( why ) Bit order G7 ... G0, R7 ... R0, B7 ... B0 MSB of the value first The original WS2812 specifies 0.35, 0.7, 0.8 and 0.6 µs, each ±150 ns, and the same reset and order; the driver values above fall inside both parts' windows. The driver column is what the examples on this site pass to the constructor, not the Kconfig default ( Configuration ). sequenceDiagram participant E as ESP32 (RMT) participant L0 as LED 0 participant L1 as LED 1 E->>L0: 24 bits for LED 0, then 24 for LED 1 L0->>L0: keep the first 24 bits L0->>L1: forward the rest through DOUT E->>L0: line low for more than 50 µs L0->>L0: latch: new colour shows L1->>L1: latch: new colour shows Signal timing turns these numbers into ticks, frame times and memory. Logic levels ¶ Parameter WS2812B At VDD = 5 V VIH, input high 0.7 × VDD minimum 3.5 V VIL, input low 0.3 × VDD maximum 1.5 V Input voltage −0.5 V to VDD + 0.5 V 3.3 V data into a 5 V strip An ESP32's 3.3 V high is under the 3.5 V the datasheet asks for. Many strips accept it on a short wire, some do not, and the margin shrinks with temperature and cable length. Use a buffer powered from 5 V that accepts 3.3 V inputs (74AHCT125, 74HCT245) between the GPIO and DIN. Power ¶ Item Value Source VDD 3.5 V to 5.3 V WS2812B datasheet Current at full white About 60 mA per LED Three LEDs at 20 mA each, from the WS2812 datasheet; the WS2812B datasheet gives no figure Decoupling 100 nF at each LED WS2812B application circuit (most strips have it) Operating temperature −25 °C to +80 °C WS2812B datasheet Budget the supply for the strip: 60 LEDs at full white is about 3.6 A. Brightness scaling lowers it in proportion. Feed long strips from both ends or every metre or so, so the far LEDs do not dim or shift colour. Adafruit's NeoPixel guide adds two parts that protect the first LED: a 300 Ω to 500 Ω resistor in series with DIN, close to the strip, and a large capacitor (1000 µF or so) across the supply at the strip input. Connect the ground before the supply, and power the strip before or with the ESP32, never drive DIN of an unpowered strip. docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to an ESP-IDF project. It is an ESP-IDF component; it does not build without ESP-IDF. Requirements ¶ Requirement Value Why Chip An ESP32-family chip with an RMT peripheral The driver transmits through the RMT ESP-IDF v5.3 or later The component requires esp_driver_rmt , which ESP-IDF split out in v5.3 C++ C++20 ( -std=gnu++20 , set by the component) Tested ESP32-C6, ESP-IDF v5.5 What the ESP32 examples CI builds The manifest idf_component.yml lists the ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3, ESP32-C6 and ESP32-H2. All of them have an RMT peripheral, but only the ESP32-C6 is built in CI. Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to a version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver.git external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver git submodule update --init external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , Kconfig and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples have their own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ); you do not need it to use the driver. ESP-IDF component ¶ Component wrapper (recommended) Repository as a component The wrapper in examples/esp32/components/hf_ws2812_rmt/ is what the ESP32 examples and CI use. Copy the folder into your project's components/ and tell it where the driver is, in your project's top-level CMakeLists.txt , before include($ENV{IDF_PATH}/...) : set ( HF_WS2812_RMT_ROOT ${ CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR } /external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver CACHE PATH "WS2812 driver checkout" ) The wrapper stops with a clear message when the path is wrong. Your component then declares REQUIRES hf_ws2812_rmt . The repository's root CMakeLists.txt registers an ESP-IDF component when ESP_PLATFORM is set, with the root Kconfig . Clone or link the repository into components/ (or add its parent folder to EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS ) and require it by its folder name. CI does not build this path. Both register the same sources and the same Kconfig menu, HF-ESP32-WS2812-RMT Configuration ( Configuration ), and require the ESP-IDF components driver , freertos and esp_driver_rmt . How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/hf_ws2812_rmt_build_settings.cmake Sources, include directories, ESP-IDF requirements, version: the single source of truth Root CMakeLists.txt ESP-IDF component when ESP_PLATFORM is set; otherwise a static library for the host tests ESP-IDF examples/esp32/components/hf_ws2812_rmt/CMakeLists.txt Component wrapper over the same settings Outside ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt only builds with HF_WS2812_RMT_BUILD_TESTS=ON , which supplies stubs of the ESP-IDF headers ( Testing and CI ). It is not a way to run the driver on a PC. The version is set once in the settings file and written into ws2812_version.h at configure time. Read it at run time: void print_version () { std :: printf ( "hf-ws2812-rmt-driver %s \n " , WS2812Strip :: GetDriverVersion ()); } Next ¶ Quickstart wires a strip and lights it; Configuration lists the Kconfig options and constructor arguments.

docs.text: Porting ¶ What runs where: the driver is ESP-IDF code for the ESP32 family. This page lists the chips it supports, what binds it to ESP-IDF, and what using it elsewhere would take. Why there is no port to write ¶ The other HardFOC drivers talk to a chip over SPI, I2C or UART, so they ask you for a small class that moves bytes, and run on any MCU. A WS2812 has no bus: it needs a pulse train timed to about 100 ns for the whole frame. On an ESP32 the RMT peripheral generates it from a buffer of symbols. This driver is built around that peripheral and calls ESP-IDF's RMT driver directly; there is no interface between the two for you to implement. Supported chips ¶ The component manifest lists these targets. The channel and memory figures are ESP-IDF's ( soc_caps.h , v5.5). Chip Transmit channels Symbols per block ESP32 8 (any channel) 64 ESP32-S2 4 (any channel) 64 ESP32-S3 4 48 ESP32-C3 2 48 ESP32-C6 2 48 ESP32-H2 2 48 CI builds the examples for the ESP32-C6 with ESP-IDF v5.5; the other chips are listed by the manifest but not built. Each WS2812Strip asks ESP-IDF for one transmit channel with 64 symbols of memory. Where a block holds 48 symbols, that request takes two blocks, which can leave the next channel without memory: on the two-channel chips, plan for one strip until you have checked a second one on hardware. Chips without an RMT peripheral (the ESP32-C2, for example) cannot run it. ESP-IDF v5.3 or later is required, because the component requires esp_driver_rmt . What is bound to ESP-IDF ¶ File ESP-IDF dependency inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp The RMT TX and RX driver, encoders, esp_check.h , esp_log.h , FreeRTOS queues inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp , src/ws2812_cpp.cpp gpio_num_t , esp_err_t , rmt_symbol_word_t , Kconfig defaults ( sdkconfig.h ) inc/ws2812_effects.hpp , inc/ws2812_multi_animator.hpp Only through WS2812Strip inc/ws2812_control.h , src/*.c The RMT driver and Kconfig, directly The effects and the bit encoding in WS2812Strip::Show() are plain C++; the ESP-IDF parts are the channel in ws2812::RmtTx and the types in the public headers. Using it on another MCU ¶ There is no supported path. Doing it means: Replacing ws2812::RmtTx with a transmitter for your MCU that sends a buffer of (high time, low time) pairs: a timer with DMA, an SPI peripheral clocked so that a few SPI bits make one WS2812 bit, or a PIO block. Replacing the ESP-IDF types in the public headers ( gpio_num_t , esp_err_t , rmt_symbol_word_t ) and the Kconfig defaults. The host build in tests/stubs/ shows the full set of ESP-IDF names the driver uses: it is a starting point, not a port. For a non-ESP32 project, a library written for your MCU's timing peripheral is usually less work. Using it on any ESP32 ¶ Nothing to write: the component wrapper builds it. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each strip one owner task, or guard every call on a strip and its animators with one mutex. docs.text: Quickstart ¶ Light a WS2812B strip from an ESP32: wire three signals, add the component, write one loop. ESP32 and ESP-IDF only The driver calls ESP-IDF's RMT driver directly. You need an ESP32-family chip with an RMT peripheral and ESP-IDF v5.3 or later; CI builds the examples for the ESP32-C6 with ESP-IDF v5.5. 1. Wire it ¶ ESP32 Strip Notes GPIO (GPIO8 in the example) DIN of the first LED Through a 3.3 V to 5 V level shifter; see below GND GND (VSS) One ground for the ESP32, the strip and its supply 5 V (VDD) From a supply sized for the strip: up to about 60 mA per LED at full white A WS2812B powered from 5 V needs at least 3.5 V (0.7 × VDD) on DIN to see a high. An ESP32 drives 3.3 V, which is below that: it often works on a short wire, but it is out of specification. A 74AHCT125 or 74HCT245 powered from 5 V fixes it. Hardware has the pin table, the power budget and the protection parts. 2. Add the driver ¶ Add the repository as a submodule and copy the ESP-IDF component wrapper into your project's components/ folder. Installation has the details and the alternatives. git submodule add https://github.com/hardfoc/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver.git external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver cp -r external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver/examples/esp32/components/hf_ws2812_rmt components/ Tell the wrapper where the driver is, in your top-level CMakeLists.txt before the project.cmake include, and add hf_ws2812_rmt to the REQUIRES of your main component: set ( HF_WS2812_RMT_ROOT ${ CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR } /external/hf-ws2812-rmt-driver CACHE PATH "WS2812 driver checkout" ) 3. Light it ¶ main.cpp #include "esp_log.h" #include "freertos/FreeRTOS.h" #include "freertos/task.h" #include "ws2812_cpp.hpp" // WS2812B bit timing in RMT ticks of 100 ns (the driver runs the RMT at 10 MHz). constexpr uint16_t kT0H = 4 , kT1H = 8 , kT0L = 9 , kT1L = 5 ; // A WS2812B reads green first: pack colours as 0xGGRRBB. constexpr uint32_t Grb ( uint8_t r , uint8_t g , uint8_t b ) { return ( uint32_t { g } << 16 ) | ( uint32_t { r } << 8 ) | b ; } extern "C" void app_main () { // 8 LEDs on GPIO8, brightness 32 of 255. The constructor claims an RMT TX channel. WS2812Strip strip ( GPIO_NUM_8 , -1 , 8 , LedType :: RGB , kT0H , kT1H , kT0L , kT1L , 32 ); for ( uint32_t i = 0 ;; i = ( i + 1 ) % strip . Length ()) { strip . SetPixel ( i , Grb ( 255 , 0 , 0 )); // one red LED walks along the strip if ( strip . Show () != ESP_OK ) { // blocks until the frame is on the wire ESP_LOGE ( "leds" , "RMT transmit failed" ); } strip . SetPixel ( i , 0 ); vTaskDelay ( pdMS_TO_TICKS ( 100 )); } } What each step does: The WS2812Strip constructor creates an RMT transmit channel on the GPIO at 10 MHz, so the four timing arguments are in ticks of 100 ns: 4, 8, 9 and 5 give 400, 800, 900 and 500 ns, inside the WS2812B's ±150 ns window. Pass them explicitly: the Kconfig defaults are not WS2812B timings ( Configuration ). Grb() packs a colour the way the strip sends it: the driver sends the packed value most significant byte first, and a WS2812B expects green first. SetPixel() writes the buffer; nothing reaches the LEDs until Show() , which scales by the brightness, encodes 24 symbols per LED and blocks until the RMT has sent them. The host CI compiles this example against the driver's headers, so it matches the current API. If it does not work ¶ Symptom First thing to check Every LED white or full on The timing arguments: ticks are 100 ns, so the Kconfig defaults (14, 52, 52, 52) are far too long Red and green swapped Colour packing: a WS2812B wants 0xGGRRBB Nothing lights Ground shared with the strip, data into DIN (not DOUT), the GPIO number First LED flickers or shows random colours Data level: add the level shifter, keep the data wire short Abort at start-up in RmtTx No free RMT transmit channel, or an invalid GPIO ( Troubleshooting ) Next ¶ API guide : brightness, resizing, effects, several strips, errors. Signal timing : how the ticks, frame time and reset gap work. Hardware : level shifting, power injection, protection parts.

docs.text: Signal timing ¶ How the driver turns pixels into pulses: ticks, the time a frame takes, the memory it needs and the reset gap. Ticks ¶ WS2812Strip runs its RMT channel at 10 MHz, so every duration it sends is a whole number of 100 ns ticks. The four timing arguments ( t0h , t1h , t0l , t1l ) are those tick counts, used as they are: the driver does not convert from nanoseconds. Pulse Driver value WS2812B window 0 bit high, t0h 4: 400 ns 250-550 ns 0 bit low, t0l 9: 900 ns 700-1000 ns 1 bit high, t1h 8: 800 ns 650-950 ns 1 bit low, t1l 5: 500 ns 300-600 ns Any value inside the window works; the LED samples the line roughly in the middle of the bit, so the difference between a short and a long high pulse is what matters. Values from the Kconfig defaults (14, 52, 52, 52) are 1.4 µs and 5.2 µs: every bit reads as a 1. ws2812::RmtTx::TransmitWs2812() , the lower-level byte path, has its own fixed timing for 10 MHz: 400 / 900 ns for a 0 and 800 / 500 ns for a 1, the same as the table. Frame time ¶ Each LED takes 24 bits (32 for RGBW). With the timing above every bit lasts 1.3 µs: LEDs RGB frame Highest refresh rate 8 0.25 ms about 3300 Hz 60 1.9 ms about 520 Hz 144 4.5 ms about 220 Hz 300 9.4 ms about 106 Hz An RGBW frame is a third longer (32 bits instead of 24). The refresh rate allows for the frame and the 50 µs reset gap. These numbers are derived from the bit time, not measured; Show() also spends CPU time building the symbols before the transfer starts. Show() blocks the calling task until the last symbol is out ( rmt_tx_wait_all_done() with no timeout). Call it from a task that can afford the wait, never from an interrupt. Memory ¶ Buffer Bytes per LED Pixels ( uint32_t ) 4 RMT symbols, RGB (24 × 4 bytes) 96 RMT symbols, RGBW (32 × 4 bytes) 128 A 60-LED RGB strip needs 6000 bytes. Both are std::vector s allocated when the strip is created or resized. The RMT channel itself has 64 symbols of hardware memory and no DMA; ESP-IDF refills it from an interrupt while a frame is sent. A refill delayed by a long critical section stretches a low period, which the LEDs read as a reset or a wrong bit. If you see glitches under heavy interrupt load, keep strips short or send frames from a high-priority task. The reset gap ¶ A WS2812B shows the new colours once its data line has stayed low for more than 50 µs. WS2812Strip::Show() does not append a reset pulse: after the last bit the RMT leaves the line low, and the LEDs latch when the next Show() starts late enough. Any frame loop with a delay (an animation tick of a few milliseconds) gives that gap on its own. Two Show() calls back to back on a short strip may not; put at least 50 µs between them. The C interface's encoder ( led_strip_encoder.c ) appends a 50 µs low symbol after each frame. Colour order ¶ Show() sends the packed 24-bit value most significant bit first: bits 23-16, then 15-8, then 7-0. A WS2812B reads green, red, blue, so pack colours as 0xGGRRBB , as the Grb() helper in the Quickstart does. For an RGBW strip the white byte (bits 31-24) goes first, then bits 23-0 in the same order. ColorWheel() and the effects pack 0xRRGGBB , so on a WS2812B their red and green are swapped; the rainbow is still a rainbow, at a different hue offset.

ColorWheel() and the effects pack 0xRRGGBB , so on a WS2812B their red and green are swapped; the rainbow is still a rainbow, at a different hue offset.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms you may see when bringing up a WS2812 strip with this driver, their causes and the fix for each. Start with the cheapest check: a common ground, data into DIN of the first LED, and the timing arguments. Most faults are one of those three. Every LED is white, or full on in one colour ¶ Cause. The bit timing. WS2812Strip counts in ticks of 100 ns; with the Kconfig defaults (14, 52, 52, 52) every high pulse lasts at least 1.4 µs, and the LEDs read every bit as a 1. Fix. Pass WS2812B timing to the constructor ( 4, 8, 9, 5 ) or put it in sdkconfig.defaults ( Configuration ). Red and green are swapped ¶ Cause. Colour order. The driver sends the packed value most significant byte first; a WS2812B expects green, then red, then blue. Fix. Pack colours as 0xGGRRBB ( Colour order ). The built-in effects and ColorWheel() pack 0xRRGGBB , so their colours are swapped the same way. Nothing lights ¶ Check How Ground The ESP32, the strip and the strip's supply share one ground Direction Data goes into DIN of the first LED, not DOUT of the last Supply 3.5 V to 5.3 V at the strip; measure at the far end under load GPIO The pin passed to the constructor is the one wired; it is an output on your chip Brightness Not 0, and not left at 0 by a Breath effect you stopped Show() Called after SetPixel() , and its result is ESP_OK The first LED flickers or shows random colours; the rest follow it ¶ Cause. The data level or the wire. A 3.3 V high is below the WS2812B's 3.5 V threshold at 5 V, and a long or unterminated data wire rings. Fix. Add a 5 V buffer such as a 74AHCT125, keep the data wire short, and put a 300 Ω to 500 Ω resistor in series with DIN at the strip ( Hardware ). The last LEDs keep old colours, or frames merge ¶ Cause. The reset gap. Show() does not send a reset pulse; the LEDs latch only after the line has been low for more than 50 µs. Two Show() calls in a tight loop may not leave that gap. Fix. Delay at least 50 µs between frames; any animation tick does ( Signal timing ). Colours fade or shift towards the far end ¶ Cause. Voltage drop along the strip at high current. Fix. Lower the brightness, or feed the supply in at both ends or every metre or so ( Hardware ). The program aborts when a strip is created ¶ Cause. ws2812::RmtTx creates its channel with ESP_ERROR_CHECK : an RMT error aborts with a backtrace that names rmt_new_tx_channel , rmt_enable or rmt_new_copy_encoder . Usual reasons: no free transmit channel (each strip takes one, and on chips with 48-symbol blocks one strip can take two blocks), an invalid GPIO, or out of memory. Fix. Create fewer strips, check the GPIO, and see Supported chips for the channel counts. Glitches while Wi-Fi or other interrupts are busy ¶ Cause. The RMT channel has 64 symbols of memory and no DMA; ESP-IDF refills it from an interrupt during a frame. A late refill stretches a low period. Fix. Keep strips short, send frames from a high-priority task, and avoid long critical sections while Show() runs ( Signal timing ). The C functions in ws2812_control.h send garbage ¶ Cause. A defect in this version: ws2812_write_leds() passes its RMT symbol buffer to a byte encoder. Fix. Use WS2812Strip ( API guide ).

From pixels to pulses, on ESP-IDF ¶ From pixels to pulses, on ESP-IDF Figure description and sources From top to bottom. Your application, the only code you write, either runs an effect or sets pixels itself. The effects (WS2812Animator and WS2812MultiAnimator, the Effect values listed from inc/ws2812_effects.hpp) draw into a WS2812Strip. The strip (inc/ws2812_cpp.hpp, public methods listed) keeps the pixel buffer, applies the brightness and turns every bit into one RMT symbol with the configured high and low times. ws2812::RmtTx (inc/rmt_wrapper.hpp) owns one RMT transmit channel at 10 MHz and sends the symbols, blocking until they are out. Below it is ESP-IDF's RMT driver (the calls listed from rmt_wrapper.hpp) and the RMT peripheral, which times the pulses on the GPIO that feeds the first LED.
